scope_note: No finite source can enumerate literally every crypto strategy ever created. This is a source-linked catalog of the principal strategy families and the short-horizon signals most relevant to a five-minute leveraged-perps decision. None is a guaranteed-profit method; the useful/not-useful fields describe regimes to test, not promises.

answer_summary.best_candidates_for_testing: For a five-minute SOL-perp horizon, test only regime-conditional setups: (1) trend continuation after VWAP/EMA/volume alignment, (2) volatility-squeeze breakout with confirmation, and (3) range mean-reversion or failed-breakout reversal when trend strength is low. RSI, MACD, Bollinger Bands, ATR, VWAP, volume/flow and ADX are filters/confluence—not standalone forecasts.
answer_summary.main_limit: A signal can be conditionally useful when market state is stable and liquid, but no indicator reliably predicts the next five-minute candle across all regimes. Leverage changes the loss distribution; it does not improve forecast accuracy.

jupiter_perps_context.execution_model: Jupiter SOL JLP Perps use oracle-priced execution rather than an order book; trades are processed by a keeper within slippage tolerance, and a price-impact fee compensates liquidity providers for large or imbalanced trades.
jupiter_perps_context.base_fee: 0.06% of trade size when opening or closing
jupiter_perps_context.borrow_fee: Accrues continuously on the full position size; it counts against collateral and moves liquidation closer over time.
jupiter_perps_context.liquidation_penalty: All remaining collateral is taken as a liquidation fee after loss, close fee and borrow fees.

regime_identification.how_to_identify: Price holds one side of VWAP; fast and slow EMA slope/stack in the same direction; ADX is rising rather than flat; pullbacks hold prior breakout structure; volume expands on impulse and contracts on pullback. Favor continuation, not countertrend RSI fades.

VWAP is relatively flat; price repeatedly rejects established support/resistance; ADX is weak; Bollinger Bands are not expanding; RSI/Stochastic reaches extremes and then turns while price remains inside the range.

Bollinger bandwidth/realized ATR contracts, the range becomes obvious, then a candle closes outside it with above-average volume and the next bar accepts outside rather than immediately reclaiming the range.

Large candle relative to ATR, rapidly widening spreads or order-book imbalance, price-impact/flow fee rising, immediate event/news risk, or price near liquidation. Reduce size or do not trade; do not convert an overbought/oversold reading into an automatic reversal.

execution_checklist.rule: Define the invalidation price before entry; size from the stop and account-risk budget, not from the maximum leverage slider.
Require expected gross move to exceed round-trip base fees, price impact, borrow cost, spread/slippage and a safety buffer.
Use a higher-timeframe regime filter (for example 15m/1h structure) and a 1m/5m trigger; do not let a single five-minute indicator decide direction.

Prefer limit/conditional orders only when their trigger and execution behavior are understood; Jupiter documents that fast movement can make triggered orders fail on slippage and that stop execution is not guaranteed near liquidation.
Backtest with fees, latency, failed/partial execution and adverse selection; paper trade or use minimal size until the edge survives out-of-sample data.

strategies.name: Trend following / moving-average crossover
strategies.formula: SMA_n = (sum of the last n closes)/n; enter long when a fast MA crosses above a slow MA (for example, 50 above 200), and exit/reverse on the opposite cross.
strategies.description: Follows an established directional move rather than forecasting a reversal; the golden cross is a commonly named bullish version.
strategies.useful_when: Sustained bull or bear trends; the MA smooths noise and confirms direction.
strategies.not_useful_when: Sideways/choppy markets or immediately after a move has already matured; lag can create late entries and whipsaws.

strategies.name: Mean reversion
strategies.formula: z = (P - MA_n)/SD_n; buy when price is sufficiently below its mean and sell/short when sufficiently above it, with an exit near the mean.
strategies.description: Bets that an unusually stretched price returns toward its historical average; common implementations use RSI or Bollinger Bands.
strategies.useful_when: Range-bound markets with repeated oscillation around a stable mean.
strategies.not_useful_when: Strong trends, where an oversold/overbought condition can persist and losses compound without a hard stop.

strategies.name: Breakout / momentum
strategies.formula: Long when close_t > highest high of the prior n bars (or above resistance); short when close_t < lowest low of prior n bars; stop back inside the range.
strategies.description: Attempts to capture the expansion that follows a consolidation range, ideally confirmed by volume and volatility expansion.
strategies.useful_when: A tight range, triangle, or volatility squeeze resolves with a decisive close and strong volume.
strategies.not_useful_when: Low-liquidity markets or false breakouts that quickly return inside the prior range.

strategies.name: Range / grid trading
strategies.formula: Place staggered buy orders at levels P0 - kΔ and sell orders at P0 + kΔ within a defined range; realized gross profit per completed grid interval is approximately Δ × quantity, before fees and slippage.
strategies.description: Systematically buys lower and sells higher inside an assumed trading range.
strategies.useful_when: A liquid asset oscillates repeatedly between well-defined support and resistance.
strategies.not_useful_when: A one-way breakout or gap leaves inventory trapped while price trends outside the grid.

strategies.name: Scalping
strategies.formula: Expected net trade = target move - fees - spread - slippage; take many short-duration trades with small targets and stops.
strategies.description: Seeks many small intraday gains, often on 1–15 minute charts, using rapid momentum or pullback signals.
strategies.useful_when: Highly liquid, tight-spread pairs with sufficient intraday movement and reliable execution/automation.
strategies.not_useful_when: Thin markets, high fees, latency, or volatile spikes; costs can consume the small target and leverage magnifies losses.

strategies.name: Swing trading
strategies.formula: No single formula; a typical rule combines a trend filter (e.g., SMA/EMA), a retracement level, and a predefined stop/target over multi-day moves.
strategies.description: Holds positions for a portion of a larger move, commonly using moving averages, Fibonacci retracements, and volume breakouts.
strategies.useful_when: Multi-day trends or clearly defined pullbacks provide room for a move without constant monitoring.
strategies.not_useful_when: Very short horizons, news-driven gaps, or directionless chop that repeatedly reverses before the target.

strategies.name: Dollar-cost averaging (DCA)
strategies.formula: Invest a fixed cash amount A at each interval; units bought each interval = A/P_t; average cost = total cash invested / total units acquired.
strategies.description: Builds exposure in equal cash installments regardless of price rather than attempting to time one entry.
strategies.useful_when: Long-term accumulation, regular income, and a desire to reduce timing/emotional risk in a volatile asset.
strategies.not_useful_when: Short-term profit objectives, a permanently declining asset, or when the investor cannot tolerate drawdowns.

strategies.name: Cross-exchange arbitrage
strategies.formula: Net profit ≈ (sell price on expensive venue - buy price on cheap venue) × quantity - trading fees - transfer/borrow costs - slippage.
strategies.description: Buys the same crypto where it is cheaper and sells where it is more expensive; spatial arbitrage is the cross-exchange form.
strategies.useful_when: A simultaneous executable spread exceeds all costs and both venues have sufficient liquidity and operational access.
strategies.not_useful_when: Spreads vanish, transfers are slow, withdrawals are halted, liquidity is thin, or counterparty/settlement risk dominates.

strategies.name: Funding-rate arbitrage / cash-and-carry
strategies.formula: Long spot and short perpetual when perp premium is attractive; approximate funding income = notional × funding rate per funding interval, less spot/perp costs and hedge slippage.
strategies.description: Pairs a spot position with the opposite perpetual-futures position to collect funding and/or profit from futures–spot convergence.
strategies.useful_when: The funding/spread is large enough to cover fees, financing, basis risk, and margin; the paper describes trading beyond a cost-adjusted no-arbitrage bound.
strategies.not_useful_when: Funding turns adverse, the spread widens before convergence, margin/liquidation risk is high, or there is no defined unwind date; the paper explicitly notes it is not risk-free.

strategies.name: Triangular arbitrage
strategies.formula: Execute A→B→C→A when (rate_AB × rate_BC × rate_CA) × (1-fee)^3 > 1; profit is the excess after all fees and slippage.
strategies.description: Exploits inconsistent exchange rates among three trading pairs on the same venue.
strategies.useful_when: The price-cycle discrepancy is larger than three legs of transaction costs and orders can be executed atomically enough.
strategies.not_useful_when: Latency, partial fills, order-book depth, or fees erase the discrepancy before the cycle completes.

strategies.name: Five-minute trend continuation (VWAP + momentum + volume)
strategies.formula: Long only when price > session VWAP, fast EMA > slow EMA, and breakout-bar volume > its rolling average; short under the mirrored conditions. Exit at a volatility-scaled target/stop or when price closes back through VWAP.
strategies.description: A rules-based continuation scalp: it does not try to call every turn; it waits for alignment between direction, intraday value, and participation.
strategies.useful_when: A directional, liquid session is already underway and the breakout/pullback is accompanied by expanding volume.
strategies.not_useful_when: Flat ranges, late-stage extensions, thin liquidity, or headline-driven reversals; signals lag and a five-minute target can be smaller than fees and slippage.

strategies.name: Liquidity-sweep / failed-breakout reversal
strategies.formula: For a long: price briefly breaks a prior low, then closes back inside the range while sell pressure fails to continue; enter only after reclaim, with stop beyond the sweep extreme. Mirror for a short.
strategies.description: Attempts to trade a failed move through an obvious prior high/low rather than blindly buying the first breakout.
strategies.useful_when: A well-defined range has repeated equal highs/lows, price briefly pierces the level, and the reclaim occurs with enough liquidity to exit.
strategies.not_useful_when: The move is a genuine news or liquidation breakout, the market is thin, or the stop is too close to Jupiter liquidation.

strategies.name: Jupiter long/short-flow imbalance filter
strategies.formula: Recent imbalance = net long-minus-short flow over roughly the last minute; opening a long or closing a short adds to it, while opening a short or closing a long subtracts. Prefer trades that reduce an existing extreme imbalance; be cautious when your trade would increase it.
strategies.description: A venue-specific positioning/flow filter. Jupiter documents that additive price impact depends on whether a trade worsens the recent imbalance and whether it is above the asset threshold.
strategies.useful_when: You can observe the live fee/price-impact estimate and want to avoid entering on the crowded side or paying an imbalance-driven fee.
strategies.not_useful_when: The flow window changes abruptly, the imbalance is not predictive of price direction, or the apparent edge is smaller than fees and execution risk.

strategies.name: Volatility-squeeze breakout
strategies.formula: Compute Bollinger bandwidth = (upper band - lower band) / middle band. Watch for unusually low bandwidth, then trade only a confirmed close outside the range with rising volume; stop back inside the range.
strategies.description: Uses compressed realized volatility as a setup and direction/volume confirmation as the trigger.
strategies.useful_when: The market has compressed into a liquid range and a decisive expansion begins.
strategies.not_useful_when: The market remains compressed, a breakout has no participation, or a headline creates a gap that bypasses a controlled stop.

strategies.name: Risk-first leveraged scalp / liquidation-distance gating
strategies.formula: Position notional = collateral × leverage; approximate unlevered PnL = notional × price_return. Size so the planned stop is reached well before the liquidation price, and require expected move > round-trip fees + spread + slippage + safety buffer.
strategies.description: Not a directional predictor; it is the gate that determines whether a five-minute signal is tradable at all.
strategies.useful_when: Every leveraged trade, especially when volatility expands or the position is above 10x leverage.
strategies.not_useful_when: It is treated as a substitute for an entry edge, or when a fast market can jump through the stop before execution.

indicators.name: Relative Strength Index (RSI)
indicators.formula: RSI = 100 - 100/(1+RS), where RS = average gain over n periods / average loss over n periods (commonly n=14).
indicators.description: A 0–100 momentum oscillator; readings below 30 are commonly called oversold and above 70 overbought, while divergences compare price highs/lows with RSI highs/lows.
indicators.useful_when: Range trading, pullback timing, and divergence/confluence with support or resistance.
indicators.not_useful_when: Strong trends, where RSI can remain overbought or oversold and premature reversal trades lose.

indicators.name: MACD
indicators.formula: MACD line = EMA_fast - EMA_slow; signal line = EMA_m(MACD); histogram = MACD - signal (standard settings often 12, 26, 9).
indicators.description: Trend/momentum indicator using a MACD line, signal line, and histogram; crossovers and zero-line moves are common signals.
indicators.useful_when: Trend confirmation, momentum shifts, and divergence analysis with price or RSI.
indicators.not_useful_when: Flat, noisy markets where repeated crossovers whipsaw, or fast reversals where the EMA signal lags.

indicators.name: Bollinger Bands
indicators.formula: Middle = SMA_n; upper = SMA_n + k·SD_n; lower = SMA_n - k·SD_n, commonly n=20 and k=2.
indicators.description: A moving-average centerline with volatility bands that widen and contract with standard deviation.
indicators.useful_when: Mean reversion at extreme bands, trend riding between middle/outer bands, and spotting volatility compression before breakouts.
indicators.not_useful_when: A strong trend that walks a band, or low-liquidity/one-off spikes where a band touch is not a reversal signal.

indicators.name: Stochastic oscillator
indicators.description: Measures the close relative to the recent high-low range; overbought is commonly above 80 and oversold below 20.
indicators.useful_when: Timing pullbacks within an existing trend and identifying potential reversals via %K/%D crossovers or divergence.
indicators.not_useful_when: Strong one-way trends, when it can stay overbought/oversold and signal too early.

indicators.name: On-Balance Volume (OBV)
indicators.formula: OBV_t = OBV_{t-1}+V_t if close_t>close_{t-1}; OBV_{t-1}-V_t if close_t<close_{t-1}; unchanged if equal.
indicators.description: Cumulative directional volume measure used to assess whether volume is confirming price direction.
indicators.useful_when: Breakout confirmation, accumulation/distribution clues, and divergence where OBV leads or contradicts price.
indicators.not_useful_when: Volume is fragmented or anomalous, or a single large print dominates cumulative history.

indicators.name: Average Directional Index (ADX)
indicators.formula: ADX_n = smoothed average of DX, where DX = 100·|+DI - -DI|/(+DI + -DI); +DI and -DI derive from smoothed directional movement divided by ATR.
indicators.description: Measures trend strength on a 0–100 scale rather than direction; the cited guide treats readings above 25 as a strong trend indication.
indicators.useful_when: Selecting trend-following versus range strategies and filtering weak breakouts.
indicators.not_useful_when: Determining long versus short by itself, or during abrupt regime changes before smoothing catches up.

indicators.name: Average True Range (ATR)
indicators.formula: TR_t = max(H_t-L_t, |H_t-C_{t-1}|, |L_t-C_{t-1}|); ATR is a moving average of TR, commonly 14 periods.
indicators.description: Measures realized price volatility, not direction.
indicators.useful_when: Setting volatility-scaled stops/targets, position sizing, and checking whether a market has enough movement for scalping.
indicators.not_useful_when: As a directional buy/sell signal by itself, or when a sudden event makes historical volatility unrepresentative.

indicators.name: Fibonacci retracement
indicators.formula: Retracement level = swing high - r·(swing high - swing low) for an up move (or the mirrored form for a down move), commonly r ∈ {0.236, 0.382, 0.5, 0.618, 0.786}.
indicators.description: Projects percentage pullback levels from a selected swing high and low to identify possible support/resistance.
indicators.useful_when: Planning entries, stops, or targets during a pullback that respects a clear prior swing.
indicators.not_useful_when: The swing anchors are subjective, the market is news-driven, or levels are treated as guarantees rather than zones.

indicators.name: VWAP
indicators.formula: VWAP = sum(price_t × volume_t) / sum(volume_t), usually calculated cumulatively over the chosen session/window.
indicators.description: Volume-weighted average traded price used as an execution benchmark and contextual support/resistance reference.
indicators.useful_when: Intraday mean-reversion or trend context, especially when price is materially above/below VWAP and other evidence agrees.
indicators.not_useful_when: Across incompatible sessions, in very thin markets, or as a stand-alone prediction of future price.

indicators.name: Ichimoku Cloud
indicators.formula: Tenkan=(9-period high+low)/2; Kijun=(26-period high+low)/2; Senkou A=(Tenkan+Kijun)/2 shifted 26; Senkou B=(52-period high+low)/2 shifted 26; Chikou=close shifted back 26.
indicators.description: Multi-line trend, momentum, and support/resistance framework whose cloud compares projected ranges.
indicators.useful_when: A multi-timeframe trend filter and for locating dynamic support/resistance in orderly markets.
indicators.not_useful_when: Very short-term scalping, abrupt regime changes, or when many overlapping lines create false precision.

indicators.name: Order-flow imbalance / aggressive-volume delta
indicators.formula: OFI_window = aggressive buy volume - aggressive sell volume over a short window; normalize by total volume or recent average. A positive value means buy aggression dominated in that window.
indicators.description: Measures who is crossing the spread now. On Jupiter, the documented recent long/short flow imbalance is also used in additive price-impact fees, so flow can matter both for signal context and execution cost.
indicators.useful_when: A liquid market is moving with persistent one-sided prints and price accepts above/below a level.
indicators.not_useful_when: Large isolated prints, fragmented venue flow, spoofing, or a market where the oracle/keeper execution is not synchronized with the observed order book.
